prOriginal.nota: Found via `gh api repos/grafana/grafana/commits/<sha>/pulls` on the benchmark commits; its last commit is the benchmark head 1cab4143d4 (squash merge 3ba2457a70), title 'Query splitting: Interpolate queries at the start of the process'. Loki plugin later moved out of grafana/grafana by #129092 (2026-07-27) to grafana/grafana-loki-datasource; today's code was read there.

advanced-query-processing-architecture-g.reason: In grafana/grafana the lines stayed unchanged until PR #129092 (2026-07-27) moved the Loki plugin to the official grafana/grafana-loki-datasource repo, still bundled with Grafana. There, on main today, runSplitQuery and runShardSplitQuery still map targets through applyTemplateVariables (templateSrv.replace + addAdHocFilters), sub-requests still carry request.filters into datasource.runQuery -> super.query, and DataSourceWithBackend.query in grafana main still calls applyTemplateVariables again, so the double interpolation and ad hoc filters remain. A move, not a fix or a removal of the behaviour.

astra.pergunta: grafana/grafana#129092 (2026-07-27) deleted the Loki core plugin and moved it to the official grafana/grafana-loki-datasource repo (still bundled with Grafana), where runSplitQuery/runShardSplitQuery are byte-identical to the benchmark head. Pendente or descontinuado?
astra.resposta: Pendente for both: #129092 moved the plugin to its official successor, still bundled, rather than eliminating the behaviour; both bugs persist there unchanged.

advanced-query-processing-architecture-g.reason: runShardSplitQuery on grafana-loki-datasource main (the successor of the deleted grafana/grafana file, moved by #129092 on 2026-07-27) still filters `query.expr` and `!query.hide` on the raw targets before `.map(applyTemplateVariables)`, exactly as at the benchmark head. No commit after the merge touched this order in either repo.

astra.resposta: Pendente for both: #129092 moved the plugin to its official successor, still bundled, rather than eliminating the behaviour; both bugs persist there unchanged.
